keywords.def: unpleasant feeling on your skin / feeling something unpleasant on your skin
rub your nails back and forth against something, often to relieve an itch
animal, plant or fungus that lives on another lifeform and feeds on it
get an illness or feeling from someone else

sentences.en: Hello and welcome to 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听 BBC Learning English 的《6 Minute English》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Georgie. Find the vocabulary, definitions and a free worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我是 Neil。我是 Georgie。你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到词汇、释义以及免费的练习题。

sentences.en: So, Georgie we're going to talk about something a little different today.
sentences.zh: Georgie，今天我们要聊一个稍微有点不一样的话题。

sentences.en: We're talking about itching. Now an itch is that unpleasant feeling you get on your skin that you have to scratch with your fingers.
sentences.zh: 我们要聊的是'痒'(itching)。itch(痒)指的是皮肤上那种让人不舒服的感觉，让你忍不住要用手指去挠。

sentences.en: What sort of things make you itch? Well, funny you should ask, because I'm actually wearing quite an itchy jumper at the moment and it's making me want to scratch my skin.
sentences.zh: 什么东西会让你感到痒呢？哈，说来也巧，我现在身上穿的这件毛衣就挺痒的，让我忍不住想挠皮肤。

sentences.en: What about you? Well, recently I was bitten by a mosquito and, as you know, when you get bitten by a mosquito, it's really itchy.
sentences.zh: 你呢？我最近被蚊子咬了，你知道的，被蚊子咬了之后真的特别痒。

sentences.en: I had to scratch loads and loads. Oh, I hate it when that happens.
sentences.zh: 我不得不使劲地挠个不停。哦，我最讨厌这种情况了。

sentences.en: It was horrible. In this podcast, we're going to hear from some experts about why we itch and how scratching can be good for us.
sentences.zh: 太难受了。在这期播客中，我们将听几位专家讲讲，我们为什么会感到痒，以及挠痒对我们来说为什么其实是件好事。

sentences.en: And as usual, we'll be learning some useful new vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 像往常一样，我们也会学习一些实用的新词汇。

sentences.en: OK. Well, we're going to start with a quiz question of course, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 好的，Georgie，我们当然还是要先来一道测验题。

sentences.en: It's a bit of a different one today. Dr Henning Holle studies the psychology of itching, and he played some scratching sounds to the guests on the BBC World Service programme CrowdScience.
sentences.zh: 今天这道题有点特别。Henning Holle 博士专门研究'痒'的心理学，他在 BBC 世界服务频道节目《CrowdScience》中，给嘉宾们播放了一些挠痒的声音。

sentences.en: Now the question is, what is being scratched?
sentences.zh: 问题来了：被挠的到底是什么？

sentences.en: You have three choices: a) an arm, b) a beard, or c) some jeans.
sentences.zh: 有三个选项：a) 手臂？b) 胡子？还是 c) 牛仔裤？

sentences.en: OK. Well, let's listen...
sentences.zh: 好，我们来听一听……

sentences.en: Well, that sounded a bit hairy, so I'm going to go with b) a beard.
sentences.zh: 嗯，听起来有点毛茸茸的感觉，所以我选 b) 胡子。

sentences.en: Well, we'll find out at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 好，答案我们会在节目最后揭晓。

sentences.en: So, Neil, I mentioned that my jumper was a bit itchy but sometimes I feel itchy for no particular reason.
sentences.zh: Neil，我刚才提到我的毛衣有点扎人发痒，但有时候我会莫名其妙地感到痒，没有什么特别的原因。

sentences.en: So, what's going on there? Well, that's something that the listeners of BBC World Service programme CrowdScience also wondered.
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事呢？其实，BBC 世界服务频道节目《CrowdScience》的听众们也曾有过同样的疑问。

sentences.en: They wanted to know the answer to that. The presenter, Anand Jagatia, spoke to itching expert Sonja Ständer to find out more.
sentences.zh: 他们也想知道答案。节目主持人 Anand Jagatia 采访了'痒'研究专家 Sonja Ständer，以进一步了解这个问题。

sentences.en: Let's listen. There's lots of science to unpack here.
sentences.zh: 我们一起来听听。这里面有很多科学原理值得细细解读(unpack)。

sentences.en: Sonja, what actually is itchiness? So, by scratching the skin, we remove parasites or plants or anything that does not belong on the skin.
sentences.zh: Sonja，痒到底是什么？其实，通过挠皮肤，我们能够去除寄生虫、植物碎屑，或者任何不该出现在皮肤上的东西。

sentences.en: And so, we start to scratch at the very same area where we itch and remove it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们会在感到痒的那个部位挠痒，把这些东西去除掉。

sentences.en: And it can no longer damage the skin and harm ourselves.
sentences.zh: 这样它们就无法再损伤皮肤、伤害我们自己了。

sentences.en: Anand says there's a lot of science to unpack about itchiness.
sentences.zh: Anand 说，关于'痒'这件事，有很多科学原理值得细细解读(unpack)。

sentences.en: Unpack here means explain. Sonja explains that when our skin feels itchy, we scratch it, and that helps to get rid of parasites and other harmful things on our skin.
sentences.zh: 这里的 unpack 意思是'解释、阐明'。Sonja 解释说，当皮肤感到痒时，我们会去挠它，这有助于清除皮肤上的寄生虫和其他有害物质。

sentences.en: Parasites are animals or plants that live on another animal and feed from them.
sentences.zh: parasites(寄生虫)指的是寄生在其他动物身上，并从中获取养分的动物或植物。

sentences.en: So, Neil, itching is our skin's way of protecting itself against harmful parasites.
sentences.zh: 所以，Neil，痒其实是皮肤用来抵御有害寄生虫的一种自我保护方式。

sentences.en: And I have to say, all of this talk of itching and scratching is making me feel a bit itchy right now.
sentences.zh: 不得不说，这么一直聊'痒'和'挠痒'，现在我自己都觉得有点痒了。

sentences.en: Well, that's interesting because Dr Henning Holle wanted to study whether just thinking about itching makes us more likely to feel itchy.
sentences.zh: 这倒挺有意思的，因为 Henning Holle 博士想研究的正是：仅仅是想到'痒'这件事，是否就会让人更容易感到痒。

sentences.en: Henning and his team studied what happened when people watched videos of itching and scratching.
sentences.zh: Henning 和他的团队研究了人们在观看挠痒视频时会有怎样的反应。

sentences.en: Let's listen to him speaking to BBC World Service programme CrowdScience.
sentences.zh: 我们一起来听听他在 BBC 世界服务频道节目《CrowdScience》中的讲述。

sentences.en: And what we found in this study was, yes, these scratching videos indeed made people feel itchier.
sentences.zh: 我们在这项研究中发现，没错，这些挠痒视频确实会让人感觉更痒。

sentences.en: They also started to scratch themselves more spontaneously.
sentences.zh: 人们也会更自发地(spontaneously)开始挠自己。

sentences.en: So, the answer is basically yes, you can catch a scratch.
sentences.zh: 所以答案基本上是肯定的：痒(scratch)是会'传染'的。

sentences.en: In Henning's study, when people watched videos of scratching, they scratched themselves spontaneously.
sentences.zh: 在 Henning 的研究中，人们在观看挠痒视频时，会不由自主地挠起自己来。

sentences.en: If you do something spontaneously, you do it without being asked or without thinking.
sentences.zh: 如果你 spontaneously(自发地)做某事，意思就是你没有被要求、也没有经过思考就做了这件事。

sentences.en: So, Henning concludes that yes, you can catch a scratch, just like you might catch an illness.
sentences.zh: 所以 Henning 得出的结论是：没错，'痒'是会传染的，就像你可能会'染上'一种疾病一样。

sentences.en: Catch in this context means get from someone else.
sentences.zh: 在这里，catch 的意思是从别人那里'感染'到。

sentences.en: OK. Georgie, I think it's time for the answer to my quiz question.
sentences.zh: 好了，Georgie，我想是时候公布我那道测验题的答案了。

sentences.en: We had a clip of people scratching and you had to decide what is being scratched.
sentences.zh: 我们听了一段人们挠痒的录音，你需要判断被挠的到底是什么。

sentences.en: I said that was a beard. OK. Well, let's see if the people who are listening to this on the programme CrowdScience agreed.
sentences.zh: 我猜的是胡子。好，我们来看看《CrowdScience》节目里的听众是不是也这么认为。

sentences.en: Sonja Ständer It sounds like hairy skin so I would go for the scalp.
sentences.zh: Sonja Ständer：听起来像是毛茸茸的皮肤，所以我会选头皮。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's beard or something because it does sound like there's hair there.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得是胡子之类的，因为听起来确实像是有毛发。

sentences.en: It is definitely hairy skin and Anand was spot on.
sentences.zh: 这确实是毛茸茸的皮肤，而 Anand 猜得完全正确。

sentences.en: So, it is indeed a beard scratch that we were listening to.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们听到的的确是挠胡子的声音。

sentences.en: Wow! So I was right! You were. Congratulations!
sentences.zh: 哇！那我猜对了！没错，恭喜你！

sentences.en: OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we learned in this programme, starting with itch, which is an unpleasant feeling on your skin.
sentences.zh: 好，我们来回顾一下这期节目学到的词汇，先从 itch(痒)开始，指的是皮肤上一种让人不舒服的感觉。

sentences.en: And something can be described using the adjective itchy.
sentences.zh: 而某样东西可以用形容词 itchy(发痒的)来形容。

sentences.en: When you feel an itch, you often scratch it with your fingers by rubbing your nails on the skin.
sentences.zh: 当你感到痒时，通常会用手指去挠，也就是用指甲在皮肤上摩擦。

sentences.en: If you unpack an idea or scientific concept, you explain it in clear detail.
sentences.zh: 如果你 unpack 一个想法或科学概念，意思就是详细清楚地解释它。

sentences.en: A parasite is an animal or plant that lives on another animal and feeds on it.
sentences.zh: parasite(寄生虫)是指寄生在其他动物身上，并以其为食的动物或植物。

sentences.en: If you do something spontaneously, you do it without being asked or without thinking.
sentences.zh: 如果你 spontaneously(自发地)做某事，意思就是你没有被要求、也没有经过思考就做了这件事。

sentences.en: Catch can be used to mean get from someone else, such as an illness.
sentences.zh: catch 可以用来表示从别人那里'感染'到某样东西，比如一种疾病。

sentences.en: For example, you can catch a cold. Once again, our six minutes are up, but you can test what you've learned with the worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 比如，你可能会'染上'感冒(catch a cold)。六分钟又到了，不过你可以用我们网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上的练习题，检验一下自己学到的内容。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us and goodbye. Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听，再见。再见。
